For complex or important messages, set the draft aside for a day or two, then start with the **big picture** (does it meet your goals?) before readability, clarity and conciseness.
Focus first on **content, organisation, style and tone**.

en: **Readability indexes** measure word length, syllables, sentence length and paragraph length only. They cannot measure design, the “you” attitude, sentence structure, transitions or word usage.
Senior managers **skim** for key ideas, conclusions and recommendations; read closely later if valuable. Four techniques: vary sentence length, short paragraphs, lists/bullets, headings.
ms: **Indeks kebolehbacaan** hanya ukur panjang perkataan, suku kata, ayat dan perenggan. Tidak mengukur reka bentuk, sikap “you”, peralihan.
Pengurus kanan **mengimbas** idea utama, kesimpulan dan cadangan. Empat teknik: variasi ayat, perenggan pendek, senarai, tajuk.

blocks.en: Four techniques: **vary sentence length**, **keep paragraphs short**, **use lists**, and **add headings and subheadings**.
blocks.ms: Empat teknik: **ubah panjang ayat**, **pastikan perenggan pendek**, **guna senarai**, dan **tambah tajuk dan subtajuk**.

en: **Paragraphs:** 100 words or fewer; inviting to the reader; connect ideas; emphasise key ideas; divide large subjects; don’t go overboard — Short paragraphs (**100 words or fewer**) are inviting and can emphasise ideas. Use one-sentence paragraphs only occasionally; use transitions when splitting subjects.

**Lists:** set off important ideas; simplify and break down complex subjects; highlight sequences of ideas — Show sequence, heighten impact and help skimming. Bullets are preferred unless there is a sequence/ranking or you refer to items. Set off with blank lines, introduce clearly, keep items **parallel**.

**Headings:** organise lengthy material; grab attention; increase understanding; group related paragraphs; visually indicate shifts — Serve three functions: **organisation**, **attention**, **connection** (main vs subordinate ideas).
ms: **Perenggan:** 100 perkataan atau kurang; menarik pembaca; sambung idea; tekankan idea utama; bahagi subjek besar; jangan keterlaluan — Perenggan pendek (**100 patah atau kurang**) menarik. Perenggan satu ayat sekali-sekala; guna peralihan.

**Senarai:** tonjolkan idea penting; ringkaskan dan pecahkan subjek kompleks; serlahkan urutan idea — Menunjuk urutan dan memudahkan imbasan. Bullet diutamakan kecuali ada urutan. Items mesti **selari**.
**Tajuk:** susun bahan panjang; tarik perhatian; tingkat kefahaman; kumpul perenggan berkaitan; tunjuk peralihan secara visual — Ada tiga fungsi: **organisasi**, **perhatian**, **hubungan**.

**Long**: best for complex ideas, multiple related points, summarising or previewing; harder to understand and skim.

en: Break up overly long sentences — You may be expressing two dissimilar thoughts or too much evidence at once.
Rewrite hedging sentences — Too many “may/seems” make you sound unsure.
Impose parallelism — Same grammatical construction shows ideas are related and equal.
Correct dangling modifiers — Modifier phrase must connect to the subject.
Reword long noun sequences — Use one word or move nouns to a modifying phrase.
Replace camouflaged verbs — (-ion, -tion, -ing, -ment, -ant, -ent, -ence, -ance, -ency) that turn verbs into nouns.
Clarify sentence structure — Keep subject and predicate close; place modifiers next to words they modify.
Clarify awkward references — Avoid “as mentioned above”, “the former/latter”, “respectively”; use a specific pointer.

blocks.en: **Production quality** (page/screen design, graphics, typography) affects effectiveness and conveys professionalism. Good design sets tone and guides readers.

en: Consistency — Margins, typeface, type size, space and recurring elements, within and across messages.
Balance — Subjective; formal grid or informal flow can both be balanced; can be too formal, just right or too informal.
Detail — E.g. very wide columns are hard to read; split into two columns.
ms: Konsistensi — Jidar, taip muka, saiz, ruang.
Keseimbangan — Subjektif; formal atau tidak formal.
Perincian — Lajur terlalu lebar sukar dibaca.

en: White space — = any blank area (margins, indents, around images and headings, between columns and lines). Provides contrast and resting points; be generous.
Margins — Justified, flush left/ragged right (most business documents), flush right/ragged left, or centred.
Typefaces — = design of the characters; **font** = collection of characters in that design. Classic: sans serif for headings, serif for body; many modern documents are all sans serif.
Type styles — (bold, italic, underline, colour): avoid styles that hinder reading.
ms: Ruang putih — = kawasan kosong. Beri kontras dan rehat; murah hati.
Margin — Dijustifikasi, rata kiri/kanan berombak (kebanyakan dokumen), rata kanan, atau tengah.
Jenis taip (typefaces) — = reka huruf; **font** = koleksi aksara. Klasik: sans serif untuk tajuk, serif untuk teks.
Gaya taip — Elak yang mengganggu bacaan.

en: Formal letters use **letterhead** (company name, address, contact details).

**Memos**: title (Memo/Memorandum/Interoffice Correspondence), then **Date, To, From, Subject**; no salutation, close or signature (initials by From line); less private because often distributed without envelopes.
**Mobile formatting**: think in small chunks; generous white space with short paragraphs (4–6 lines); format simply; consider horizontal and vertical layouts.
ms: **Memo**: tajuk, kemudian **Date, To, From, Subject**; tiada salam/penutup/tandatangan; kurang peribadi.
**Format mudah alih**: bahagian kecil; ruang putih; perenggan 4–6 baris; format ringkas; layout menegak dan mendatar.

en: Proofreading is the **quality inspection** stage and your last chance before your message and reputation reach the audience; even a small mistake can doom your efforts.

Look for two kinds of problems: (1) undetected errors from writing, design and layout; (2) errors during production (missing fonts, broken web links, printing ink problems). Be extra vigilant with complex documents involving many people and computers.
Details to check: language errors, missing material, design errors, typographical errors.
ms: Pembacaan pruf ialah peringkat **pemeriksaan kualiti** dan peluang terakhir.
Dua jenis masalah: (1) ralat penulisan, reka bentuk, layout; (2) ralat semasa pengeluaran (font hilang, pautan rosak).
Semak: ralat bahasa, bahan hilang, ralat reka bentuk, ralat taip.

en: Make multiple passes — , focusing on one aspect each time (content, then layout).
Use perceptual tricks — , because your brain supplies missing pieces: read backward bottom to top; finger under each word; slit in paper to reveal one line; read aloud pronouncing each word.
Double-check high-priority items — Names, dates, addresses, numbers (e.g. $5,000 vs $50,000).
Give yourself some distance — Before proofreading.
Be vigilant — Not in long sittings or when tired.
Review complex digital documents on paper — **Review complex digital documents on paper**.
Take your time — Quick is not careful.

blocks.en: Time needed depends on length and complexity: a typo in a team email is minor, but in a financial report, contract or medical file it can be serious.

en: **Cost**: printing, binding and delivering reports can be expensive; weigh cost against benefit. Overnight delivery could look responsive or wasteful depending on the situation.
**Convenience**: effort for you and the audience; ensure recipients can expand compressed files; for very large files use DVDs or file-hosting sites.
**Time**: how soon must it arrive? Don’t pay for overnight delivery if it won’t be read for a week; don’t mark messages “urgent” unless truly urgent.

**Security and privacy**: weigh convenience against risk; sensitive messages restrict recipients and means; people are wary of attachments, so convert word-processor files to **PDF** (more immune to viruses).
ms: **Kos**: cetak, jilid dan hantar mahal; timbang kos dan manfaat.

**Masa**: berapa segera? Jangan tanda “urgent” jika tidak benar-benar.
**Keselamatan dan privasi**: pertimbangkan risiko; tukar fail kepada **PDF** (lebih kebal virus).

q.en: Explain four techniques to improve the readability of a business message.

en: Vary sentence length: short up to 15, medium 15–25, long over 25 words (2)
Keep paragraphs short: 100 words or fewer, emphasise key ideas (2)
Use lists to set off ideas and simplify (2)
Add headings and subheadings to organise and show shifts (2)
ms: Ubah panjang ayat: pendek hingga 15, sederhana 15–25, panjang lebih 25 (2)

Tambah tajuk untuk susun dan tunjuk peralihan (2)
